equity_bridge.item: Equity investments at book (income excluded from EBITDA; matching-asset rule)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K balance sheet, LIN.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:2553; income from equity investments $150m FY2025 sits below operating profit and is not in the flows
30 Sep 2026, LIN.DE_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:245,253; flows are 100% consolidated so NCI is deducted here once

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management guidance and underlying trend: Q3-2026 underlying sales +5% (3% price, 2% volume) plus backlog start-ups; FY2026 adjusted EPS guided +8-9%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-1.5% 3yr, -4.2% 5yr) because Linde returns more than it earns ($4-5bn/yr buybacks plus $2.8bn dividends against $6.9bn net income); it diverges >30% from the EPS CAGR (21-25%, off a FY2020/FY2022 base depressed by merger charges and the 2022 Russia/Amur impairments) and is not a usable growth proxy. Revenue 3yr CAGR of 0.6% is cost pass-through deflation (FY2022 carried peak energy pass-through) -- underlying sales grew mid-single digits. Selected 6.0% NTM growth is anchored to guidance, not to any of the CAGRs
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped: net debt $22.8bn, no cash pile to double-count). FY2020 3,896 -> FY2022 5,584 -> FY2025 4,925 ($m). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-4.1%) is below reported (-3.7%) only marginally -- SBC is 0.5% of sales and stable. The FCF decline since FY2022 is entirely growth capex ($3.2bn -> $5.3bn) against a $11bn backlog; OCF rose from $8.9bn to $10.4bn over the same period

scenario_narratives.base: Linde compounds as it has for the past decade: ~5% underlying sales growth (3% price, 2% volume) plus project start-ups from the $11bn backlog in the early years, decelerating to 3% by year 9. The reported EBITDA margin edges from 38% to 39% on pricing above inflation and productivity (cost-reduction charges continue to recur and are kept inside the margin). Capex normalises from the FY2026 peak of 15.5% of sales to 12.5% as the sale-of-gas projects move into operation. The terminal value is bound by the 20x FCF cap in every scenario, which is the house's answer to the ~30x free cash flow the market currently pays for this quality; the required-return table shows what the price implies.
scenario_narratives.bull: Backlog converts and keeps refilling (electronics and clean energy), volumes run 4-5%, reported EBITDA margin reaches 40%, capex intensity returns to 12% and terminal growth is 3.5%. Same 8% WACC: the upside is in the flows, not in a lower discount rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: Industrial-volume stagnation in Europe and softer US/China manufacturing; growth is price only (3%), margins compress to 36% on pass-through and restructuring, capex stays at 13% because the committed projects are built regardless, terminal growth 2%. No balance-sheet stress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on consolidated USD flows, converted to EUR at the dated spot rate. SBC expensed, share count flat, NCI deducted once at book, equity investments added at book because their income is outside EBITDA. Terminal value is min(Gordon, 20x FCF) and the cap binds in all three scenarios, so the valuation is effectively 'ten years of owner FCF at 8% plus a 20x exit'. The gap between the house value and the market price is the price of Linde's quality premium (~30x FCF, ~29x adjusted EPS); the required-return table states the IRR the current price implies rather than arguing the cap should be higher.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex intensity does not normalise: if the backlog keeps refilling at $10bn+ and capex stays at 15% of sales, year-10 FCF is ~15% lower than the base path
USD/EUR: a 10% move in the dollar moves the EUR value per share 10%; the DCF is in USD
Terminal multiple: the 20x cap is the whole argument -- at the market's ~30x the base value would be ~40% higher
Cost pass-through and energy prices distort reported revenue growth and margin in both directions (FY2022-23 showed +/-5pp swings)
Project returns: sale-of-gas contracts are take-or-pay, but customer credit (chemicals, clean hydrogen start-ups) and start-up delays can push returns below the ~12-13% historical level
Cost-reduction charges ($40m-$600m per year) are treated as recurring inside the margin; the adjusted-EPS guidance excludes them

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for LIN.DE at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 332.4-479.4 EUR. Parity-checked against the Nasdaq LIN USD close via EURUSD=X (see inputs.fx_note)
data_sources.financials: LIN.DE_Metrics.csv (FY2017-FY2025 annuals, quarterlies to Q3-2026); FY2025 Form 10-K (LIN.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt) for income taxes paid, SBC, equity investments, leases, diluted shares; Q3-2026 earnings release (LIN.DE_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt) for the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet, net debt, diluted shares, NCI and FY2026 guidance
data_sources.qualitative: Q3-2026 release (segment commentary, backlog, guidance) and FY2025 10-K MD&A. LIN.DE_Analysis.json was being generated in parallel and was not available at build time

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back $164m (LIN.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:2605), scaled to TTM revenue (~0.47% of sales). Linde publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-award-tax figure; net-share-settlement taxes are not separately disclosed, so the add-back is used as is
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 30 Sep 2026 net purchases of ordinary shares: FY2025 $4,601m + 9M-2026 $2,632m - 9M-2025 $3,211m. The flat diluted count is funded: Linde retires ~2%/yr net of issuance, well above the ~0.5% SBC grant rate
inputs.share_count_basis: Q3-2026 weighted-average diluted shares 462.512m (LIN.DE_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:209); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are USD (Linde plc files with the SEC in US dollars; LIN.DE is the Xetra EUR line). Per-share values computed in USD and converted at USD/EUR 0.8956 (= 1 / EURUSD 1.1166, Yahoo EURUSD=X, 2026-10-30T21:29Z). Parity check: Nasdaq LIN $514.24 at the 2026-10-30 US close / 1.1166 = EUR 460.5 against the observed Xetra close of EUR 462.0, a 0.3% tie that confirms the rate, its direction and the quote basis
inputs.fy0_note: Base revenue is the trailing twelve months to 30 Sep 2026: FY2025 $33,986m + 9M-2026 $27,474m - 9M-2025 $25,222m = $36,238m. Year 1 is therefore the next twelve months (roughly FY2027), discounted one full period. FY2026E on the Q4 guide is ~$36.9bn
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Sep 2026: short-term debt 4,645 + current LTD 1,464 + long-term debt 20,593 = 26,702 less cash 3,947 = 22,755, which ties to the company's own 'Net debt 22,755' (LIN.DE_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:611). Finance leases (~$214m) are inside total debt; operating lease liabilities (~$866m) are NOT, because the operating lease cost is expensed inside EBIT
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year UST ~4.2% (Oct 2026) + 0.85 beta x 5.0% ERP = ~8.5% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (A-rated, 2025-26 issuance), ~3.6% after tax; ~10% debt weight at market values (net debt $22.8bn vs ~$240bn equity) gives ~7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the flows (growth, margin, capex paths), not stacked in the discount rate
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are expensed as operating cost inside EBIT under ASC 842 (treatment B: cost in the flows, operating lease liabilities of ~$866m excluded from net debt). Finance leases (~$214m) are in total debt and their ROU depreciation is inside D&A, which is consistent with carrying them as debt. Not charged twice
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled on a consolidated (100%) basis; non-controlling interests are deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book ($1,563m NCI + $10m redeemable NCI at 30 Sep 2026). NCI takes ~$160m/yr of a $7.1bn net income (2.3%), so book is a fair proxy. FY2025 reported attributable net income $6,898m ties to modelled NOPAT less after-tax interest within non-operating noise
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is reported EBITDA (operating profit + D&A) PLUS the SBC add-back, because the engine deducts SBC separately. FY2025: (8,923 + 3,763 + 164) / 33,986 = 37.8%; 9M-2026 reported 36.5% + 0.5% SBC = 37.0%, depressed by ~$600m of Q3 cost-reduction and other charges; adjusted (ex-charges, ex-purchase-accounting) operating margin is ~29.4% which is ~40% EBITDA. Cost-reduction charges recur at Linde every year ($40m-$600m), so the base path sits at a reported-basis 38-39%, not the adjusted ~40%. Income from equity investments (~$150m/yr) is excluded from EBITDA and its source asset is added back in the bridge
inputs.cash_tax_basis: Income taxes paid FY2025 $2,274m / operating profit $8,923m = 25.5% (10-K 'Income Taxes Paid' table, LIN.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:3120); FY2024 $2,216m / $8,635m = 25.7%. Effective book rate 22.4% but the unlevered EBIT base is higher than pre-tax income. 25% applied to EBIT in all years
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials'), built from USD flows and converted to the EUR quote. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF and no memory entry. Linde is the world's largest industrial-gas company: ~$34-37bn of sales across Americas/APAC/EMEA/Engineering, roughly two-thirds on-site and merchant volumes under long-term take-or-pay contracts with cost pass-through, ~30% adjusted operating margin and a $11bn sale-of-gas project backlog (electronics, clean energy, chemicals). FY2026 guidance (Q3 release, 29 Oct 2026): adjusted EPS $17.82-17.92 (+8-9%), capex $5.5-6.0bn. The valuation hinges on three things: (1) the capex intensity, which at 15-16% of sales is ~2.5pp above the FY2021-23 run-rate because of the backlog and is assumed to normalise to 12.5% as projects start up; (2) whether the 20x terminal FCF cap is the right exit for a business the market currently pays ~30x free cash flow for -- the house cap binds in every scenario, and the required-return table is the honest readout of what the current price implies; (3) the USD/EUR rate, which moves the EUR value one-for-one. SBC is tiny (0.5% of sales) so the house/street band is narrow. Analysis JSON was not available when this build ran; qualitative axes are drawn from the Q3-2026 release and FY2025 10-K

bear.narrative: European industrial demand stays weak (EMEA volumes +1% in Q3-2026), US/China manufacturing softens, and clean-energy project start-ups slip, so volumes run ~0-1% and growth is mostly price; the capex already committed to the backlog is spent anyway, so capex intensity stays elevated (13%) against lower returns; energy-cost pass-through and restructuring charges hold the reported margin at 36-37%. No solvency axis: A-rated, net debt 1.8x EBITDA

base.growth_note: NTM 6.5% = ~3% price + ~2% volume + ~1.5% backlog start-ups and residual FX; decelerates to 3% by year 9 as the $11bn backlog is absorbed. Consistent with the 8-9% EPS algorithm once buybacks (~2%/yr) are excluded
base.margin_note: Reported-basis EBITDA + SBC 37.8% FY2025, 37.0% 9M-2026 with heavy Q3 charges. Base ramps 38.0% -> 39.0% on price-over-inflation and productivity, below the ~40% adjusted level because cost-reduction charges recur
base.capex_note: FY2026 guide $5.5-6.0bn = ~15.5% of sales; declines to 12.5% (FY2021-23 averaged ~11-12%) as sale-of-gas projects move from construction to operation. D&A held at 10.5% (TTM 10.6%): purchase-accounting amortisation runs off while the asset base grows
base.wc_note: Negative capture (-3% of the revenue change): receivables and inventory exceed payables for a manufacturer; FY2025 working capital was a ~$200m use

bull.narrative: Electronics (semiconductor fab build-out), clean-energy and chemicals backlog converts on time and keeps refilling above $10bn; volumes run 4-5% with price 3%+; productivity and pricing take the reported EBITDA margin to 40% (adjusted ~41%); capex intensity falls back to 12% as the construction wave passes. Terminal growth 3.5% reflects a secular gases growth rate above GDP

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20% because the two live risks -- EMEA industrial weakness (volumes +1%) and the possibility that the $11bn backlog earns below the historical ~12-13% project returns in a clean-energy downturn -- are already visible in the Q3-2026 numbers, even though there is no solvency axis. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs electronics and clean-energy project cadence to stay strong simultaneously with margin expansion beyond the current adjusted ~30% operating margin, which Linde has only partly delivered since the 2018 merger synergies ran off.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
